questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Adelaide University Law School for its strong academic reputation and courses that matched my legal interests. The city’s safety, affordability, and unique cultural experiences also appealed to me. Additionally, studying abroad offered a valuable opportunity for both professional growth and personal development.

questions.answer: It wasn't easy. It is pretty complicated with a lot of steps.

questions.answer: we had some different introductions with the study abroad team, but not that much assistance

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It’s quite challenging because you’re unfamiliar with the standards, which made my housing quite expensive. I recommend reaching out to someone who has been or is currently at your destination to get advice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive, but in my case, better that the on campus. However, you can end up living with people who do not study, which does not give you the campus feeling.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It has a website familiar with the KUNET, so it was pretty doable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a very good study overseas administrator who answered quickly and was a very big help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up going to some different classes than I thought I would, since the other classes got filled very quick. But I ended up being happy with the classes I registered in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick. The "good" classes goes quick.

questions.answer: Quite easy, people are very nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and show interest

questions.answer: the students at my uni where quite young

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, openness and Sincerity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything will work out, seek help if needed and enjoy - everything goes by so fast

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience in it self

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adapting to an entirely new environment, particularly understanding and navigating differences in academic expectations and standards. Additionally, managing practical aspects like housing and finances, including unexpected costs such as high rent and bank fees, added to the difficulty. However, these challenges also provided valuable learning experiences and personal growth.
